questions.prompt: Simplify \(\delta_{ij}A_{ij}\) and express the result using matrix notation.
questions.answer:
We need to perform the indicated indexed calculation.
Method: Apply the summation convention and Kronecker-delta contraction rules.
The delta forces \(i=j\):
\[\delta_{ij}A_{ij}=A_{ii}=\sum_i A_{ii}=\operatorname{tr}A.\]
Final answer: \(\operatorname{tr}A\).

questions.prompt: Verify \(\delta_{ij}x_i y_j=\mathbf x\cdot\mathbf y\) in three dimensions.
questions.answer:

Method: Apply the summation convention and Kronecker-delta contraction rules.

Final answer: \(\delta_{ij}x_i y_j=\mathbf x\cdot\mathbf y\).

questions.prompt: Prove \(\delta_{ij}\delta_{jk}=\delta_{ik}\) from the component definition of \(\delta\).
questions.answer:
We need to perform the indicated indexed calculation.
Method: Apply the summation convention and Kronecker-delta contraction rules.
For fixed \(i,k\), the sum \(\sum_j\delta_{ij}\delta_{jk}\) can be nonzero only at \(j=i\) and \(j=k\). If \(i=k\), one term equals one; if \(i\ne k\), no term survives. Hence the sum equals \(1\) for \(i=k\) and \(0\) otherwise.
Final answer: \(\delta_{ij}\delta_{jk}=\delta_{ik}\).

Final answer: \(A_{ij}\delta_{ij}=A_{ji}\delta_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}A\).
